name: Question 6
problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=x(t)+2y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-2x(t)+5y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above. The eigenvector $v=[2,\text{ }2]^{T}$ corresponds to the repeated eigenvalue $\lambda =3$ of the system's matrix $A.$ The vector $w=[-1,\text{ }0]^{T}$ is such that $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$ Select the correct options in the reasoning below.The general solution of the system is

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}] & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]t{e}^{3t}+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{{field-1}}) \\  & ={c}_{1}{e}^{3t}{{field-2}}+{c}_{2}{e}^{3t}[\begin{aligned}2t-1 \\ 2t\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$

The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to $v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ has the equation 

$$
y={{field-3}}
$$

and the straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{1}{e}^{3t}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$
lie on that line. 

Since ${e}^{3t}\to $ 
{{field-4}} 
as $t\to \infty ,$ these solutions approach 
{{field-5}}  
as $t\to \infty .$

Let's add the solutions to the phase space.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069697/assets/c993f6fc9eb12c0d8f60c420519a7db4a5cf78da9f0c24d0ade87b0a96590f59.png)

Now, consider solutions of the form
${c}_{2}{e}^{3t}[\begin{aligned}2t-1 \\ 2t\end{aligned}].$
When ${c}_{2}=4,$ we get the following curve:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=4(2t-1){e}^{3t} \\ y={{field-6}}\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the coordinates (rounded to two decimal places) of several points on the curve, we get the table below.

| $t$ | $-0.5$ | $0$ | $0.2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | {{field-7}} | $-4$ | $-4.37$ |
